findings.claim: NIST Cybersecurity Framework v1.1: an analogy for providing a common language. The footnote says SSDF practices may support CSF outcomes but do not map to its Functions/Categories/Subcategories and are typically different parties' responsibility. [BT] (§1, p. 2 and footnote 2)
findings.source_check: What the bullet says is accurate: §1 p. 2 calls the common-language approach 'similar to the approach taken by' the CSF (source.md 385-388), and footnote 2 says SSDF practices 'may help support' CSF Functions, Categories and Subcategories 'but ... do not map to them' (399-403). But the source also uses NISTCSF as a Table 1 References key for 14 tasks: PO.1.1 ID.GV-3 (545), PO.1.2 (592), PO.1.3 ID.SC-3 (621), PO.2.1 (675), PO.2.2 PR.AT (700), PO.2.3 (741), PO.5.1 (945), PO.5.2 (995), PS.1.1 PR.AC-4/PR.DS-6/PR.IP-3 (1038), PS.2.1 (1078), PS.3.1 (1108), PW.1.1 ID.RA (1183), PW.4.1 ID.SC-2 (1341), PW.4.4 (1410). It is also a bibliography entry, Version 1.1 (2018) (2059-2062). The deep presents the CSF only as an analogy plus a no-mapping footnote. Its bullets that list Table 1's mapped references (line 211, 'the bibliography and Table 1 include ...') and the other NIST references (line 213) both leave NISTCSF out, so a reader would conclude that the CSF is not a Table 1 reference. No sentence is false. The picture is incomplete in a way that misleads.
searches: NISTCSF (source: 16 hits, 14 of them Table 1 reference rows)
findings.fix: correct: append to the bullet: "Table 1 nonetheless lists NISTCSF subcategory references for 14 tasks (e.g., PO.1.1: ID.GV-3; PS.1.1: PR.AC-4, PR.DS-6, PR.IP-3), and the References list cites the CSF as Version 1.1 (2018). [BT] (Table 1, pp. 5-13; References, p. 21)"

notes: Full read of both files, with line counts and deep sha256 matching packet.json. The deep states no practice or task counts, so there was nothing to miscount. All 19 live practice names match the source character for character. Every printed-page pointer checked out, including footnotes 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 and the Table 2 row mappings for 4e(vii), 4e(viii) and 4e(ix). No training leakage, no post-source vocabulary and no task guidance of the ingester's own were found. The 'Positions ... frames against' entry is a real opposition, because the source says 'not to create a checklist' (440-442). The deep 205 statement that the source gives no measured percentage reduction is a correct absence claim on a full read. A repairer may want to restore the 'e.g. ... agile' bound. For the repairer: Appendix C's Sept 2021 log says 'moved PW.3.2 to PW.4.5' (2285), but Table 1 says 'PW.3.2: Moved to PW.4.4' (1293).
